📝 Summary

Destiny Rings is a Bluetooth-enabled smart ring that detects nearby compatible users for dating, social, or networking purposes. Core features include mode selection (Dating/Social/Networking), proximity notifications, sending Signals, Fate Checks, and instant profile reveals to initiate in-person talks. It solves key pain points like endless app swiping, lack of real chemistry, and virtual-only matches by emphasizing physical proximity and authentic interactions. USP is replacing digital fatigue with real-world serendipity. Overall value proposition: facilitating genuine connections with people actually nearby without remote matching.

📈 Market Timing [...] ⚔️ Competition

Competition level: Medium. Direct competitors: 1. Tinder (tinder.com), 2. Bumble (bumble.com), 3. Hinge (hinge.co), 4. Happn (happn.com - location-based proximity), 5. Feeld (feeld.com - alternative dating). Advantages: Hardware-enabled passive proximity detection, immediate in-person focus with modes for different intents, avoids endless profiles. Disadvantages: Requires buying/wearing physical ring (cost and convenience barrier), smaller initial network for effective proximity matching, higher privacy/safety concerns vs. pure apps, no established brand.

Hey Product Hunt 👋  
  
I'm Jayson, founder of Destiny Rings. I built this because I was tired of the swipe-scroll-repeat cycle that dating and social apps trap you in — you match with someone, text for weeks, and half the time never actually meet.  
  
Destiny Rings flips that. You wear a Bluetooth-enabled smart ring, and when someone compatible is physically nearby — at a bar, a coffee shop, a networking event — the app lets you know in real time. Send a Signal, run a quick Fate Check, and if it's mutual, tap to reveal and start a real conversation on the spot. No more talking to someone for a month before meeting them, no more wondering if the profile photos were even recent. [...] There are three modes — Dating, Social, and Networking — so it's not just for romance. Whether you're trying to meet people at a happy hour, make friends in a new city, or connect with someone in your industry at a conference, the mechanic is the same: real proximity, real timing, real people.  
  
We're launching first in Hoboken, NJ before expanding to Jersey City and NYC. The app is live now (ring hardware is in final validation), so you can try Go Live mode today without a ring — proximity, Signals, and Fate Check all work through the app alone.  
  
Would love your feedback, especially on the onboarding flow and what would make this feel like a no-brainer to try at your next night out. Thanks for checking it out! 🙏 [...] Destiny Rings

@stella\_reed1 Great question! In dense/crowded areas, the app uses signal strength and configurable detection range to filter out noise — so instead of pinging you about everyone within 100 feet at a packed bar, it prioritizes people who are genuinely close (a few feet away) and compatible based on your preferences. You can also adjust your detection range in settings if you want it tighter or wider depending on the environment. Still very much in beta and something we're actively tuning as we get more real-world usage data — appreciate you asking, this is exactly the kind of edge case we want to get right before scaling up!

Stella Reed
